name: Invoice-cum-bill of supply
definition: Where a registered person supplies taxable AND exempted goods or services to an UNREGISTERED person, rule 46A permits one document — an invoice-cum-bill of supply — for all of those supplies, notwithstanding rule 46, rule 49 and rule 54.
why_it_exists: Without it a retail counter selling one taxed item and one exempt item to a walk-in customer would have to issue two documents for one transaction. It exists to stop the paperwork from splitting a single sale.
inputs: whether the supplies include both taxable and exempted items
preconditions: the supplier is a registered person
the recipient is an unregistered person
the supplies include taxable as well as exempted goods or services or both
exceptions: UNKNOWN — rule 46A states no exception and enumerates no particulars of its own
common_mistakes: using it for a registered recipient — rule 46A is limited to an unregistered person
using it where every item is taxable — the rule requires taxable AS WELL AS exempted supplies
assuming the rule 46 particulars are waived — rule 46A says only that a single document may be issued; it does not say what it must contain
gst_references: UNKNOWN — the particulars required on an invoice-cum-bill of supply are not stated in rule 46A and were not found elsewhere in this source
UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the registration status of the recipient
the taxable or exempt character of each line
confidence_factors: weak when the exempt lines are not distinguishable from the taxable lines on the face of the document
weak because the required particulars are not defined by the rule
validation_checks: at least one line is taxable and at least one line is exempt
REQUIRES HUMAN ACCOUNTANT before rejecting such a document for a missing particular, because rule 46A does not enumerate particulars
examples: a shop selling a taxed packaged good and an exempt unbranded good to a walk-in customer on one document
counterexamples: a document to a GSTIN-holding buyer — rule 46A does not reach a registered recipient
